questions.q: The most widely accepted and classic definition of **Democracy**, popularized by former US President Abraham Lincoln, defines it as:
options: A system where the richest citizens strictly control the nation's wealth
The government of the people, by the people, and for the people
A political system where the military holds supreme constitutional power
A government managed strictly by religious traditional leaders
questions.explain: Abraham Lincoln famously defined **Democracy** as "government of the people, by the people, for the people," emphasizing that ultimate political power fundamentally resides with the voting citizens.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Which of the following is a core **feature** of a true Democratic system?
options: Periodic, free, and fair elections
The total suppression of freedom of speech and the press
The concentration of all government powers in a single individual
Complete intolerance of minority political parties
questions.explain: A fundamental feature of any working **Democracy** is the regular conduct of **periodic, free, and fair elections**, which allows citizens to freely choose or change their leaders.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: In Nigeria, which highly important democratic institution is constitutionally mandated to organize, conduct, and supervise all national and state elections?
options: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC)
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC)
The National Youth Service Corps (NYSC)
The Nigerian Bar Association (NBA)
questions.explain: The **Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC)** is the democratic body established by the Nigerian Constitution to independently oversee and conduct elections in the country.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: What is the primary function of **Political Parties** as democratic institutions?
options: To violently protest and destroy government infrastructure during economic crises
To unite citizens with similar political ideologies to legally contest elections and form the government
To strictly administer justice and send convicted criminals to federal prisons
To legally print and distribute the nation's currency notes
questions.explain: A **Political Party** is an organized group of individuals with similar political ideologies whose primary objective is to contest elections, win political power, and form a government to implement their manifesto.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q:
Examine the table comparing two democratic institutions:

| Institution | Primary Goal |
|---|---|
| Political Party | To win elections and control government |
| Pressure Group | $X$ |

Which of the following correctly replaces $X$?
options: To overthrow the government through military coups
To influence government policies and decisions in favor of its members without seeking to form the government
To independently conduct and declare election results
To permanently replace all registered political parties
questions.explain: Unlike political parties, **Pressure Groups** (like Trade Unions) do not contest elections to form the government. Their sole aim is to influence government policies and protect the interests of their specific members.

questions.q: Democracy operates on the principle of Separation of Powers. The government is divided into three distinct **Arms**. What are they?
options: Federal, State, and Local
President, Governors, and Ministers
Executive, Legislature, and Judiciary
Army, Navy, and Air Force
questions.explain: The three constitutional arms of government designed to check and balance each other are the **Legislature** (makes laws), the **Executive** (implements laws), and the **Judiciary** (interprets laws).
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Which specific arm of a democratic government acts as the "last hope of the common man" by interpreting the law and impartially settling disputes?
options: The Executive
The Legislature
The Judiciary
The Civil Service
questions.explain: The **Judiciary** (the court system) is the arm of government responsible for interpreting laws, defending human rights, and settling disputes, making it the last hope of the common man against injustice.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: A Multi-Party system is heavily associated with modern democracy. What does this concept mean?
options: Only one political party is legally allowed to exist in the entire country
Two political parties violently fight for power without conducting elections
Several distinct political parties are legally recognized and can contest for political power
Political parties are totally banned, and only independent candidates are permitted
questions.explain: A **Multi-Party system** implies the legal existence of three or more political parties, giving the electorate a wide variety of choices and promoting healthy democratic competition.

questions.q: What is the crucial **Importance of Democracy** in a developing society?
options: It promotes good governance, ensures equality, and violently suppresses opposition
It fosters political stability, protects fundamental human rights, and allows for peaceful transitions of power
It guarantees that the wealthiest citizens permanently dominate the poor
It drastically increases arbitrary rule and dictatorship
questions.explain: Democracy is immensely important because it prevents tyranny, legally **protects fundamental human rights**, and ensures that political succession is managed through peaceful, constitutional elections rather than violence.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Both Political Parties and Pressure Groups are essential democratic institutions. However, what is the single most defining difference between them?
options: Political parties aim to win elections and form the government, while pressure groups only seek to influence government policies without contesting elections
Pressure groups only exist in military regimes, while political parties exist only in democratic systems
Political parties use violent protests exclusively, while pressure groups use the court system
Political parties are completely funded by INEC, whereas pressure groups print their own currency
questions.explain: The primary distinction is power acquisition: **Political parties** field candidates to win elections and control the government. **Pressure groups** simply lobby and pressure those already in power to enact favorable policies.
